security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel S-mode code writes an spmpcfg entry via the sireg2 indirect CSR access using only the lower 16 bits (e.g., a u16 value or value & 0xFFFF mask), causing SXLEN-16 upper WPRI bits to be zeroed instead of preserved, corrupting the full SXLEN-bit spmpcfg register state
security_spec.summary: spmpcfg redefined from a 16-bit field within an SXLEN-bit register to a full SXLEN-bit register; kernel must treat spmpcfg as SXLEN-bit on sireg2 read-modify-write to preserve WPRI bits [SXLEN-1:10]

findings.finding: SPMP (Sspmp) is not implemented in this kernel tree. CSR_SISELECT (0x150) and CSR_SIREG (0x151) are defined only for AIA interrupt controller access, not for SPMP. CSR sireg2 (0x152) is not defined at all. There is no spmpcfg CSR number allocation, no spmpaddr definition, and no code that writes spmpcfg entries through indirect CSR access. The vulnerability pattern (kernel writes spmpcfg via sireg2 with only lower 16 bits, corrupting upper WPRI bits) cannot occur because the SPMP infrastructure is entirely absent.

spec_citations.excerpt: Supervisor-level CSRs: siselect (0x150), sireg (0x151), sireg2 (0x152), sireg3 (0x153), sireg4 (0x155), sireg5 (0x156), sireg6 (0x157). CSR 0x152 (sireg2) is defined by Sscsrind as an alias for indirect CSR access, but is not defined in this kernel tree.
